deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the abandoned start of a business letter, written in pencil in Kurrent script. The faint text on the sheet reads as follows:
(1) Top right, struck through: 'Göttingen, den 4. April 1859.'
(2) Centre, struck through: a salutation, probably 'Hochgeehrter Herr Schiffsrheder!' (Most honoured Mr. Shipowner!). The last word is uncertain.
(3) Unstruck: an address line, 'Herrn L. Meinck [?] & Co. Bremen.' The firm name is uncertain.
(4) Unstruck: the date rewritten as 'Göttingen d. 4. April 1859'.
(5) Two struck-through opening phrases. These read something like 'ich habe Ihnen ... mitzutheilen' with an interlinear correction, and 'bin aber jetzt ...'.

The content suggests an aborted letter to a Bremen firm, possibly a shipowner or shipping agent, on some personal or business matter. The sheet was presumably reused for, or filed with, scientific notes; the previous folio has notes on complex functions and contour integrals. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

The page is still useful for dating. It fixes Riemann's presence in Göttingen on 4 April 1859, and it may help date neighbouring sheets in the bundle. The previous page appears to contain lecture material on complex-function theory: Cauchy–Riemann equations, path-independence of integrals, and residues, together with a lecture timetable note ('Donnerstags, Freitags und Sonnabends von 1–2 Uhr').

transcription_corrections: The struck-through salutation looks like 'Hochgeehrter Herr Schiffsrheder!' but the last word is not certain from the image; it could also be another occupational title or a name.
The firm name 'L. Meinck & Co.' is uncertain. The pencil could also be read as 'L. Meineke', 'Meinecke' or similar; the image does not settle it.

The struck line transcribed 'ich habe Ihnen mitzutheilen' is too faint to confirm. Only 'ich' at the start is reasonably clear. The interlinear addition rendered '{+ist+}' may be a different short word.
The second struck line 'bin aber jetzt' is plausible but also largely illegible.
